comments.quote:
24-Hour Security Cap: Profile updates (new registration, device binding, or UPI PIN reset) cap transactions at ₹5,000 total for the first 24 hours.
Volume Cap: Standard Default merchants (₹100k tier) are subject to a maximum 20 transactions daily per rolling 24 hours.
Bank-Level Overrides: Remitter banks reserve authority to apply lower internal spending limits (e.g., ₹50,000 daily) regardless of category cap allowance.
Note: The Standard Default tier is additionally subject to a 20-transaction daily limit per rolling 24 hours, and the ₹5,000 new-user cap described above still applies within its 24-hour window regardless of MCC.

Note: While the NPCI sets the maximum ceilings above, individual Remitter Banks reserve the right to set lower internal limits based on their own risk policies (e.g., a specific bank might cap daily UPI spends at ₹50,000 regardless of your MCC).

comments.text: Compliance recheck needed before publishing. Multiple secondary reports describe an NPCI revision effective 15 Sep 2025 that raised limits for capital markets, insurance, government e-marketplace, travel, EMI/loan collection, credit card bill payment, jewellery, forex, and digital account opening/term deposits to Rs 5,00,000 per transaction, with a separate daily aggregate cap that varies by category (Rs 10,00,000 for some, Rs 6,00,000 or Rs 5,00,000 for others, uncapped for general business payments). Two of those reports explicitly exclude Education and Healthcare from that revision, which conflicts with this table grouping them into the same Rs 500,000 High Ceiling Tier as Insurance and Government. I could not reach NPCI's own circular directly (blocked by robots.txt) or a Cashfree compliance page with this exact table, so I have not changed any figures.
